SP-CONSOLE-2 — closing report

Captured 2026-08-17, viewport 1280×900, the Nashville Doubles Classic workspace (LIVE) on the Phase-5 backend (alembic v6a1c5e8f3b4). Before set: docs/audits/2026-08-17-console-refine-report.html and the operator review PDF the directive’s item IDs point into. 26 operator surfaces; the entrant tier is out of this program’s scope (zero entrant files in the diff) and was under concurrent development at capture time.

Gates at close: make check exit 0 · vitest 1773 · pytest 1609 passed / 66 skipped · ruff clean · contrast 68/68 both themes · eslint 0 errors / 118 warnings · depcruise 0 errors / 16 warnings · tsc + entrant typecheck 0.

/ws-settings — Workspace settings

WSSET-1 (R-A): nav + H1 “Workspace settings”. WSSET-2: Save on the page-header row. WSSET-3: the Lifecycle row and the header chip are the same StatusPill family (X4).

Deliberate deviations (each with its reason — the ledger carries the long form)

  • X2 — one control-column width, not four slots. Every slot shares the right edge anyway; a per-row width knob could only vary where a control’s left edge fell, which no row wants. 240px = the widest segmented control on the ladder.
  • CFG-2 — the slider readout holds its own slot. The number boxes now sit left of their reserved unit column; aligning one slider to the boxes would misalign every slider with every other control. Boxes align with boxes.
  • PLAN-1 — fills kept, legend added. The brief offered legend or re-language; the fills are already the correct status tokens and the board’s at-a-glance read depends on them. The problem was that they were unexplained.
  • LIVE-6 — suppressed for the first slot, not the first minute. Elapsed time is slot arithmetic; a minute is not expressible at this resolution. Same intent, at the resolution the data has.
  • DC-2 — readout + link, not toggles. A toggle here would be a second place to disable a module, with its own has-data 409 path and dependency rules, and two surfaces to disagree. The ambiguity was the complaint; the rows now read unambiguously as a readout.
  • TV-7 — no bracket slide. Hybrid workspaces run two boards with different layout vocabularies (ADR 0006 non-merge); the board switch — which survives the venue render — is the route between them. A bracket slide inside the meet board would need a merged projection that does not exist.
  • TV-2 — the score lane renders empty on meet matches. By design (ruling R-C): the wire carries no per-set data for meet (D19) and the domain has no live score entry. The lane is laid out so a future score-relay app lights it up without a redesign.
  • BMAT-4 — feeder names only where a feeder exists. A feeder-less empty slot reads as “Bye” in the label helper — right for a real bye, a lie for an unbuilt round — and the list cannot tell them apart. No feeder, no claim: TBD stays.
  • WSM-3 — no change. joined_at is stamped at the membership grant and never updated; “Joined Aug 11” on an Aug 10 event is truthful — the event date is operator-chosen and unrelated.
  • B-1 — vitest baseline 1746, not the directive’s 1751. A pre-existing gate-green dead-nav removal (five assertions covering deleted exports) was committed before branching. Owner-ratified.
  • Backups — pre-migration manual snapshots stay rotation-eligible. Existing rows backfill as auto; nothing recorded which were manual. One-time, unavoidable, documented in the migration.
  • Ops scope — unified surface only. Every PLAN-*/LIVE-* change lands on the unified Operations surface the review PDF captured. The meet-only and bracket-only legacy surfaces (single-engine workspaces) keep their old treatment; widening was not in the evidence.
